Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin to Source Code. As full-time employee, max is write unless role owns the system; Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, not Source Code, so max is write. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) as contractor with basic security training (note: earlier note listed full_time; Security record shows contractor). Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training), never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read for Source Code.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The employee: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR agent note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says max is write unless role owns system; Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, not Source Code, so max is write.
- Security agent note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says Security DB shows contractor with basic security training, contractors max is read (write requires advanced training), never admin.

So there is a conflict between HR and Security notes about employment type. HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write; admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, not Source Code, so max is write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security says basic training, so max is read.

Which to trust? The Approver must use information available. Security DB typically handles access records; conflict resolution: security note says "Security DB shows contractor (note: earlier note listed full_time; Security record shows contractor)". Hmm.

As Approver, I need to make a decision. Given conflicting employment type, the safer/more restrictive level would be read. The requested level is admin, which exceeds both possible maximums. Grant maximum: either write (if full_time) or read (if contractor). Security record shows contractor, giving max read.

I think we should go with read, since security DB is authoritative for access controls and the conflict means we should be conservative. Grant read.
